## Genetical Data

```{r}
import_genet <- function(){
  # Set directory
  setwd(PROJECT_PATH)
  
  # GH marker
  diet_data_GH <- read_obifasta("metabar_PP_GH.simple.clean.c10.l40.taxo.ann.fasta")
  diet_data_GH %<>% extract_features("obitag_bestmatch","obitag_bestid","obitag_rank","scientific_name",'taxid')
  
  # 18S marker
  diet_data_18S <- read_obifasta("metabar_PP_18s.simple.clean.c10.l80.taxo.ann.fasta")
  diet_data_18S %<>% extract_features("obitag_bestmatch","obitag_bestid","obitag_rank","scientific_name",'taxid')
  
  # ITS marker
  diet_data_ITS <- read_obifasta("metabar_PP_ITS.simple.clean.c10.l180.taxo.ann.fasta")
  diet_data_ITS %<>% extract_features("obitag_bestmatch","obitag_bestid","obitag_rank","scientific_name",'taxid')
  
  # Centralize data in Named List (no duplication, just ref)
  diet_data_list <- setNames(
    list(diet_data_GH, # df
         diet_data_18S, 
         diet_data_ITS), 
    c("GH","18S","ITS") # names
  )
  
  # Return
  diet_data_list
}

extract_feature <- function(data,key){
  # Extract key (obiclean_weight, or other)
  # with ROBIFastread function
  # given the dataframe
  diet_mat <- extract_readcount(data, key=key)
  # The result is a dgCMatrix
  diet_mat
}

```

## taxid \> Famille/Genre/Espèce

```{r}

# Function Take the rank name for a give rank
get_rank <- function(x, rank) {
  val <- x$name[x$rank == rank]
  if(length(val) == 0) NA else val
}

# Fonction to create taxid ref for local genet data from ncbi
create_taxid_ref <- function(){
  # Take all unique taxid from clean genet data
  all_unique_taxid <- c(gene$GH$taxid, 
                      gene$`18S`$taxid, 
                      gene$ITS$taxid) %>% unique()
  
  # from unique taxid import list of full path
  taxo <- classification(all_unique_taxid, "ncbi")

  # Import F, G, s from taxo thanks to get.rank()
  tax_table <- map_dfr(taxo, ~tibble(
    family  = get_rank(.x, "family"),
    genus   = get_rank(.x, "genus"),
    species = get_rank(.x, "species")
  ))
  
  # remove the genus from the specie
  tax_table$species <- word(tax_table$species, 2) # keep the second word
  
  # Add taxid to FGs
  tax_table$taxid <- all_unique_taxid
  
  # Return
  tax_table
}

get_FGs <-function(data){
  # Get Familly, Genus, species from faxid reference
  data <- left_join(data, tax_table, by="taxid")
  data
}
```

### Density grid

```{r}

# 4 functions :
# - normalization
# - make_density_grid
# - bota_model_NCI
# - plot_grid
# - plot_hist

normalization <- function(count) {
  # Take : 
  # - count column
  # Do :
  # - Normalisation of count
  # Return :
  # - density column
  
  # Normalisation
  density <-  count / sum(count)
  
  # Return
  density
}

make_density_grid <- function(bota_focus, R){
  # Take : 
  # - bota_focus dataframe (Xfield, Yfield)
  # - R the radius of count around the pixel position
  # Do :
  # - Create the doublet (x,y)
  # - Add indices (i,j)
  # - Count the number of trees around each pixels in a circle of radius R
  # - Convert count to density
  # Return :
  # - The density grid in a triplet (x, y, density)
  
  # Create the doublet (x,y)
  grid <- expand.grid(
    x = seq(10,300,10), # X position of samples
    y = seq(10,400,10) # Y position of samples
    )
  # Add indices
  grid$i <- grid$x / 10
  grid$j <- grid$y / 10
  
  # Count the number of trees around each pixels in a circle of radius R
  grid$count <- pmap_int( # Apply a function to each coordinates (x,y)
  list(grid$x, grid$y), # Element of iterations
  \(x, y) sum((x - bota_focus$Xfield)^2 + # Count TRUE ...
              (y - bota_focus$Yfield)^2 <= R^2, # ... on Pytagore condition (dx²-dy² <= R²)
              na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
  # Convert count to density
  grid$density <- grid$count %>% normalization()
  
  # Return
  grid
}

bota_model_NCI <- function(bota_focus){
  # Take : 
  # - bota_focus dataframe (Xfield, Yfield)
  # Do :
  # - Create the doublet (x,y)
  # - Add indices (i,j)
  # - Euclidean distance between this pixel and all trees (dij)
  # - Keep only trees within 20 m (excluding distance 0)
  # - Compute the NCI
  # - Convert it to density
  # Return :
  # - The density grid in cols (x, y, i, j, NCI,density)
  
  # Create the doublet (x,y)
  grid <- expand.grid(
    x = seq(10, 300, 10),
    y = seq(10, 400, 10)
  )
  
  # Add indices
  grid$i <- grid$x / 10
  grid$j <- grid$y / 10
  
  # Initialize NCI column
  grid$count <- NA
  
  # Loop over rows (pixels)
  for (pixel in 1:nrow(grid)) {
    
    # Coordinates of the current pixel
    px <- grid$x[pixel]
    py <- grid$y[pixel]
    
    # Euclidean distance between this pixel and all trees
    dij <- sqrt((px - bota_focus$Xfield)^2 + 
                (py - bota_focus$Yfield)^2)
    
    # Keep only trees within 20 m (excluding distance 0)
    sel <- which(dij < 20 & dij > 0)
    
    if (length(sel) == 0) {
      grid$count[pixel] <- 0
    } else { # Compute the NCI
      grid$count[pixel] <- sum( 
        (bota_focus$CircCorr[sel]^2) * 
        exp(-0.25 * dij[sel]),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    }
  }
  
  # Convert NCI to density
  grid$density <- grid$count %>% normalization()
  
  # Return
  grid
}


plot_grid <- function(grid, col_name){
  # Take :
  # - grid : the triplet (x,y,z)
  # - col_name : the name of column for color
  # Do:
  # - Create the ggplot
  # Return :
  # - plot
  
  # Create the ggplot
  p <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = .data[[col_name]])) + # use col_name to take the column
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(fill = "Densité")
  
  # Return ggplot
  p
}

plot_hist <- function(grid,col_name){
  # Take :
  # - grid : the triplet (x,y,z)
  # - col_name : the name of column for color
  # Do:
  # - Create the ggplot
  # Return :
  # - plot
  
  # Create the ggplot histogram
  p <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = .data[[col_name]])) +
    geom_histogram() +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # Return ggplot
  p
}
```

## Filtre Gaussien

```{r}

# 2 functions of convertion :
# - col_to_img
# - img_to_col

col_to_img <- function(z){
  # Take :
  # - z : the z of the grid (x,y,z)
  # Do:
  # - Convert (z) in matrix of size (ni,nj)
  # - Convert matrix in image of size (ni,nj)
  # Return :
  # - image of imager package
  
  # Convert (z) in matrix of size (ni,nj)
  mat <- matrix(z, nrow = 30, ncol = 40, byrow = FALSE)
  
  # Convert matrix in image of size (ni,nj)
  img <- as.cimg(mat, x=30, y=40)
  
  # Return
  img
}

img_to_col <- function(img){
  # Take :
  # - img : image of imager package
  # Do:
  # - Create the doublet (x,y)
  # - Put image value in column (z)
  # Return :
  # - grid triplet (x,y,z)
  
  # Create the doublet (x,y)
  grid <- expand.grid(
    x = seq(10,300,10),
    y = seq(10,400,10)
    )
  # Put image value in column (z)
  grid$z <- as.vector(img)
  
  # Return cols
  grid
}
```

# Cluster

## MCMC (Metropolis Hasting) sur image smooth

```{r}

mcmc_sampling <- function(img,n_iter){
  # Take :
  # - img : image to sample
  # - 
  # Do :
  # - Set seed
  # - Convert img to matrix
  # - Get size of the matrix
  # - Get real x and y
  # - Set initial points (indices)
  # - Initalise samples storage
  # - MCMC loop to fill samples
  # Return:
  # - samples : postions of samples (x,y)
  
  # Set seed
  set.seed(123)
  
  # Convert img to matrix
  z <- as.matrix(img)
  
  # Get size of the matrix
  nx <- nrow(z)
  ny <- ncol(z)
  
  # Get real x and y
  x_vals <- seq(10, 10*(nx-1), length.out = nx)  # exemple correspondance i -> x
  y_vals <- seq(10, 10*(ny-1), length.out = ny)  # exemple correspondance j -> y
  
  # Set initial points (indices)
  i <- sample(1:nx, 1)
  j <- sample(1:ny, 1)
  
  # Initalise samples storage
  samples <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_iter, ncol = 2)
  
  # MCMC loop to fill samples
  for(k in 1:n_iter){
    
    # propose new point (continu)
    i_new <- i + runif(1, -1, 1)  # déplacement continu
    j_new <- j + runif(1, -1, 1)
    
    # stay inside bounds
    i_new <- max(min(i_new, nx), 1)
    j_new <- max(min(j_new, ny), 1)
    
    # interpolation bilinéaire pour obtenir z continu
    i0 <- floor(i_new); i1 <- ceiling(i_new)
    j0 <- floor(j_new); j1 <- ceiling(j_new)
    di <- i_new - i0
    dj <- j_new - j0
    
    # handle edges
    i1 <- min(i1, nx)
    j1 <- min(j1, ny)
    
    # bilinear interpolation
    z_new <- (1-di)*(1-dj)*z[i0,j0] + di*(1-dj)*z[i0,j1] +
             (1-di)*dj*z[i1,j0] + di*dj*z[i1,j1]
    
    z_current <- z[i,j]
    
    # accept/reject
    alpha <- z_new / z_current
    if(runif(1) < alpha){
      i <- i_new
      j <- j_new
    }
    
    # stocker en coordonnées réelles
    samples[k, ] <- c(
      x_vals[1] + (i-1)*(x_vals[2]-x_vals[1]),
      y_vals[1] + (j-1)*(y_vals[2]-y_vals[1])
    )
  }
  
  # Rename columns
  samples <- as.data.frame(samples) %>%
    rename("x"="V1","y"="V2")
  
  # Return
  samples
}
```

## K_means

```{r}

kmeans_clustering <- function(k, samples){
  # Take :
  # - k : number of clusters to create
  # - samples : samples position (x,y)
  # Do:
  # - Set seed
  # - Apply K-means function
  # - Add labels to dataframe
  # Return :
  # - df_kmeans : triplet dataframe (x, y, cluster)
  
  # Set seed
  set.seed(123)
  
  # Apply K-means function
  kmeans_result <- kmeans(samples, centers = k, nstart = 25)  # nstart = nombre d'initialisations
  
  # Add labels to dataframe
  df_kmeans <- data.frame(
    x = samples[,1],
    y = samples[,2],
    cluster = factor(kmeans_result$cluster)
  )
  
  # Return
  df_kmeans
}

```

## Double plot (MCMC and Clustering)

```{r}

# filtre gaussien
img <- col_to_img(grid$density) # <- TEST
img_smooth <- isoblur(img, sigma = 2) # smooth img
# Apply MCMC function
mcmc_samples <- mcmc_sampling(img_smooth,1000)
# Get MCMC plot
p1 <- ggplot(mcmc_samples, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "red", size = 0.5) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "MCMC") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 400),
    breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100))

# Apply clustering function
df_kmeans <- kmeans_clustering(20, mcmc_samples)
# Get clustering plot
p2 <- ggplot(df_kmeans, aes(x = x, y = y, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  stat_density_2d(aes(fill = cluster, group = cluster),
                  color = "black", alpha = 0.1, geom = "polygon") +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  labs(title = "K-means clustering") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 400),
    breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100))

# Plot MCMC and Clustering
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

**Problème:**

On ne peux pas différencier par arbre, mais par cluster. Un même cluster peux contenir 1 gros arbre ou plusieurs petits. On fait l'hypothèse que la taille du cluster est proportionnelle à la Basal Area des arbres qui le compose.

## Analyse Intertype

```{r}

# 1. Créer un objet ppp pour les deux types
xrange <- range(c(grid_BAG$i, grid_DIC$i))
yrange <- range(c(grid_BAG$j, grid_DIC$j))
window <- owin(xrange, yrange)

# Créer les points avec marquage
pp <- ppp(
  x = c(grid_BAG$i, grid_DIC$i),
  y = c(grid_BAG$j, grid_DIC$j),
  window = window,
  marks = factor(c(rep("type1", nrow(grid_BAG)),
                   rep("type2", nrow(grid_DIC))))
)

# 2. Calculer la fonction K-cross
Kc <- Kcross(pp, "type1", "type2")

# 3. Calculer la L-cross
Lc <- Lcross(pp, "type1", "type2")

# 4. Display
plot(Lc, main = "Analyse intertype Attraction/Répulsion")

```

## Confidence interval

```{r}
envelope_result <- envelope(
  pp,
  fun = Lcross,
  i = "type1",
  j = "type2",
  nsim = 99,       # nombre de simulations
  rank = 1,        # enveloppe 95%
  global = TRUE    # enveloppe globale
)

plot(envelope_result,
     main = "Analyse intertype avec enveloppes Monte Carlo",
     legendargs = list(x = "topleft", legend = c("Lcross", "Enveloppe 95% Monte Carlo")))

```

***Bagassa guianensis*** **et *Dicorynia guianensis* sont naturellement attirés**

# Genetical Data



## Correspondance Bota/Génèt

```{r}


create_sample_ref <- function(){
  # Import physical data of samples
  data_samples <- read.table(
    "/home/jean/Bureau/2026_Stage_ADNe/doi_10_5061_dryad_dc28m__v20181029/Zinger_et_al_metabar_PP1_samples.txt",
    header = TRUE,
    comment.char = "#"
  )
  # Select and split pcr
  sample_ref <- data_samples %>%
    select(pcr,x,y) %>%
    separate(pcr, into = c("sample_loc", "sample_rep"), sep = "_") %>%
    distinct(sample_loc, x, y)
  
  # Return Ref
  sample_ref
}

sample_seq_count <- function(genet_focus){
  # Take :
  # - genet_focus : OBITools dataframe with a taxa filter
  # Do:
  # - Extract quantitative value for each sample in a dataframe
  # - Sum all count sequence of each sample for the targeted taxa
  # - Put rownames in a new column
  # Return :
  # - sample_df : the doublet (sample_id, count)
  
  # Extract quantitative value in a matrix 
  sample_matrix <- extract_feature(genet_focus,"obiclean_weight") 
  
   # Sum all count sequence of each sample for the targeted taxa
  sample_df <- sample_matrix %>%
    rowSums() %>% # sum
    as.data.frame()
  
  # Put rownames in a new column
  sample_df$sample_id <- rownames(sample_df)
  sample_df$count <- sample_df$.
  sample_df <- sample_df %>%
    select(sample_id,count)
  
  # Return
  sample_df
}

loc_seq_count <- function(sample_df){
  # Take :
  # - sample_df : the doublet (sample_id, count)
  # Do:
  # - Mean samples count by localisation
  # - Add (x,y) with sample_ref
  # Return :
  # - loc_df : the quadruplet (sample_loc, count, x, y)
  
  # Mean samples count by localisation
  sample_df <- sample_df %>%
    separate(sample_id, into = c("sample_loc", "sample_rep"), sep = "_") %>%
    group_by(sample_loc) %>%
    summarise("count" = mean(count))
  
  # Add (x,y) with sample_ref
  loc_df <- left_join(sample_df, sample_ref, by="sample_loc")
  
  # Return
  loc_df
}

select_genet <- function(diet_data_list, Marker, Level, Name){
  # Take :
  # - diet_data_list :
  # - Marker :
  # - Level :
  # - Name :
  # Do:
  # - Select marker
  # - Get Familly, Gender, species cols
  # - Select taxa
  # Return :
  # - genet_focus :
  
  # Select marker
  genet <- diet_data_list[[Marker]]
  
  # Get Familly, Gender, species cols
  genet <- get_FGs(genet)
  
  # Select taxa
  genet_focus <- select_tax(genet, level, Name) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[level]])) # col family, genus or specie
  
  # Return
  genet_focus
}

make_genet_density_grid <- function(genet_focus){
  # Take :
  # - genet_focus :
  # Do:
  # - Get count of sequences by samples
  # - Mean sample count by localisation
  # - Normalisation
  # Return :
  # - loc_df :
  
  # Get count of sequences by samples
  sample_df <- sample_seq_count(genet_focus)
  
  # Mean sample count by localisation
  loc_df <- loc_seq_count(sample_df)
  
  # Normalisation
  loc_df$density <- normalization(loc_df$count)
  
  # Return
  loc_df
}

```

# Diganostic

## Simple count : R-squared / radius of count


```{r}

# Global Parameters
Level <- "Family"
Name <- "Fabaceae"
level <- tolower(Level) # low case for genetical
Marker <- "GH" # "18S" "ITS"

# Genet Model
## Select data
genet_focus <- select_genet(gene, Marker, Level, Name)
## Density grid
sample_df <- make_genet_density_grid(genet_focus)

R2_compute <- function(radius){
  # Bota Model
  ## Select data
  bota_focus <- select_tax(bota, Level, Name)
  ## Density grid
  grid <- make_density_grid(bota_focus, radius)
  
  # Compare density grids
  df_compare <- sample_df %>%
    rename(dens_genet = density) %>% # rename density
    left_join(grid, by = c("x", "y")) %>% # left join
    rename(dens_bota = density) %>% # rename density
    filter(!is.na(dens_bota)) %>% # Remove NA bugs from sample_ref
    mutate(err_abs = dens_genet - dens_bota)
  
  # Calcul de R^2 manuellement
  y <- df_compare$dens_genet             # Donnée de référence
  y_pred <- df_compare$dens_bota         # Prédictions du modèle
  y_mean <- mean(df_compare$dens_genet)  # Moyenne des données observées
  SS_residual <- sum((y - y_pred)^2)  # Somme des carrés des résidus
  SS_total <- sum((y - y_mean)^2)    # Somme des carrés totaux
  
  # Return
  R_squared <- 1 - (SS_residual / SS_total)
  R_squared

}

# Create the summary table
err_R_tab <- expand.grid(
  radius = seq(5,20),
  R2 = 0
)

# Fill the summary table
for (i in 1:length(err_R_tab$radius)) {
  print(R2_compute(err_R_tab$radius[i]))
  err_R_tab$R2[i] <- R2_compute(err_R_tab$radius[i])
}


ggplot(err_R_tab,aes(x = radius, y = R2)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(color = "gray"),  # Lignes des axes en noir
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),  # Texte des axes en noir
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black")  # Ticks des axes en noir
  ) + 
  labs(x = "Radius count (m)",
       y = "R-squared")
```

## From NCI to new empirical gaussian

```{r}

# Generalized density function

# Global Parameters
Level <- "Family"
Name <- "Fabaceae"
level <- tolower(Level) # low case for genetical
Marker <- "GH" # "18S" "ITS"

# Genet Model
## Select data
genet_focus <- select_genet(gene, Marker, Level, Name)
## Density grid
genet_grid <- make_genet_density_grid(genet_focus)

# Bota Model
## Select data
bota_focus <- select_tax(bota, Level, Name)

## Optimization of the bota model

### Gaussian model for botanical grid (beta parameter)
bota_gaussian <- function(BETA, GAMMA){
  # Create the doublet (x,y)
  grid <- expand.grid(
    x = seq(10, 300, 10),
    y = seq(10, 400, 10)
  )
  
  # Add indices
  grid$i <- grid$x / 10
  grid$j <- grid$y / 10
  
  # Initialize NCI column
  grid$count <- NA
  
  # Loop over rows (pixels)
  for (pixel in 1:nrow(grid)) {
    
    # Coordinates of the current pixel
    px <- grid$x[pixel]
    py <- grid$y[pixel]
    
    # Euclidean distance between this pixel and all trees
    dij <- sqrt((px - bota_focus$Xfield)^2 + 
                (py - bota_focus$Yfield)^2)
    
    # Keep only trees within 20 m (excluding distance 0)
    sel <- which(dij < 20 & dij > 0)
    
    if (length(sel) == 0) {
      grid$count[pixel] <- 0
    } else { # Compute the gaussian index
      grid$count[pixel] <- sum( 
        (pi*(bota_focus$CircCorr[sel]/2)^2) * # Basal Area
        exp(-BETA * dij[sel]^GAMMA),              # Gaussian Kernel
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    }
  }
  
  # Convert NCI to density
  grid$density <- grid$count %>% normalization()
  
  # Return
  grid
}

### Fonction to minimize
rss_function <- function(par, ADNe_obs) {
  # Prameters
  beta <- par[1]
  gamma <- par[2]
  
  # Prediction
  bota_grid <- bota_gaussian(beta, gamma)
  
  # Residuals
  resid <- ADNe_obs - bota_grid$density
  
  # RSS
  print(sum(resid^2))
  print(beta)
  sum(resid^2)
}

### Launch Optimization
res <- optim(
  par = c(0.2,1), 
  fn = rss_function,
  ADNe_obs = genet_grid$density,
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(0,0),  # logical constraint (biological)
)

### Result : Parameter
res$par
```
